Notes from a training deck:

IFRS 18 replaces IAS 1. It is effective for annual periods beginning on or after 1 January 2027 and earlier application is permitted. IFRS 18 introduces an operating profit subtotal in the statement of profit or loss. IAS 7 requires cash flows to be classified as operating, investing and financing activities. IAS 2 requires inventories to be measured at the lower of cost and net realisable value, and a write-down is reversed when the circumstances that caused it no longer exist. Under IAS 1, an entity presents current and non-current assets separately unless a liquidity presentation is more relevant. A complete set of financial statements includes a statement of cash flows. Management-defined performance measures must be disclosed in a single note under IFRS 18. The statement of changes in equity reconciles opening and closing equity. Comparative information for the preceding period is required. These rules apply to all entities using IFRS Accounting Standards, subject to local endorsement. The presentation of other comprehensive income may be in a single statement or two statements under IAS 1. IFRS 18 also introduces enhanced requirements for aggregation and disaggregation of information. Entities must review their account mapping before the effective date.
